recipes.name: Roasted Butternut Squash and Garlic Lasagna
ingredients_raw: 3 pounds butternut squash, halved and seeded
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Grease a baking sheet.
Brush butternut squash halves with vegetable oil and season with salt.
Roast in the preheated oven until golden and easily pierced with a knife, 45 to 50 minutes. Cool for 15 to 20 minutes, then scoop flesh into a bowl. Set aside.

Heat butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Cook and stir garlic in hot butter until softened. Stir in flour and cook for 3 minutes. Whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer and cook, whisking occasionally until thickened, about 10 minutes. Stir in butternut squash flesh and season with salt and pepper. Butternut sauce can be made 3 days ahead and refrigerated.
Reduce the oven temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Beat heavy cream in a large glass or metal mixing bowl until foamy. Gradually season with salt, continuing to beat until medium peaks form. Lift the beater or whisk straight up: the tip of the peak should curl over slightly. Set aside.

Pour 1 cup butternut sauce into the prepared baking dish and place 3 lasagna noodles on top in a single layer. Spread 1/2 of remaining sauce over noodles and sprinkle with 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese. Cover with another layer of noodles, spread remaining sauce on top, and sprinkle with 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese. Place final layer of noodles on top. Spread whipped cream over noodles, making sure pasta is completely covered. Sprinkle with remaining 1/3 cup Parmesan cheese. Cover the baking dish tightly with aluminum foil.
Bake for 30 minutes. Remove the foil and continue baking until the top is bubbly and golden brown, about 10 minutes. Allow to rest for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Butternut Squash and Garlic Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: Butternut squash and garlic are the stars of this rich and creamy lasagna loved by carnivores and vegetarians. Using no-boil lasagna noodles saves time!

review.reviewBody: I can't tell you all how good this was!!!! Let's just say that for Thanksgiving I had about 20 different things to eat and this was the only thing that was completely gone. Half the people there said this was their favorite. Here's what I did different: I used 12 noodles instead of 9 and dipped them in boiling water as some of the reviews said the noodles were too hard after baking. I also added more flour since my sauce was not thickening (about 2 tablespoons more). I also added one large sauteed onion to the garlic mix. This dish was beyond good and I'll be making it again and again. I was a little nervous about the heavy cream on top but it was great. I baked the lasagna for about 45 min total and then let it sit for a cpouple of hours (to be timed with dinner) and then warmed it up in the over before serving. BRAVO BRAVO BRAVO!!!!! UPDATE: Made this again. I used a Vidallia onion. It worked wonderfully. For the topping I used half and half and just stired some salt into it (didn't have a mixer where I was baking). You don't lose any bit of flavor with that sub.

We make this every week! This sauce goes well with any pasta, not just lasagna. We make a half portion and use 1 small butternut squash and 3 cloves of garlic. To speed up the cooking time, we cube the squash and roast it for 30 minutes, then mash it before adding it to the sauce. You can omit the cream topping, and the milk can be replaced with soy milk. To add some vegetables, this goes really well with zucchini, spinach, Cremini mushrooms, and peas.

Great! I did make a few adjustments. I used wontons instead of no cook lasagna noodles. Double them if you want a thicker noodle but I like the wontons b/c I don't like the thicker traditional lasagna noodles. I did add a dollop of ricotta cheese in the center of each wonton, smashing to spread it out a little. Also, sprinkle fresh basil on all the layers. I increased the creamy mixture by using 1/2 cup butter, 1/2 c. flour and 6 cups milk (3 c. whole, 3 c. 1%) I love the whipped cream topping sprinkled with parmasean. My dish browned up very nicely unlike the photo. I did forget to add freshly grated nutmeg before cooking but will sprinkle very lightly on top before serving. If one wanted a more traditional lasagna dish one could add mozzerella cheese. I did not b/c I was trying to hold down the calories. Delish dish for a cool fall or winter day! Also, good the next day!

Very good, paired with a salad of arugula, pecans, and pomegranate. Made some changes like most of the reviewers suggested. Left out the heavy cream top, added spinach, bulked up on spices with the addition of a few dashes of nutmeg and chili powder, and a pinch of clove and cinnamon. Lasagna noodles were a tad undercooked, even after I flashed boiled each pasta layer 20 seconds. This was an easy fix, I just poured some water on top and put back in the oven for 10 minutes. Thankfully, this dish is forgiving! Next time I will try adding zucchini, which I think might add enough fluid to cook the noodles. We’ll see! Dinner took around 3 hours to make, but no regrets.

I followed the recipe and suggestions, making the following modifications: whole milk subbed for all dairy (Fair Life) for lactose intolerant issues, caramelized onions and basil in the squash sauce, one layer of canned spinach - drained, no cream on top. I could eat this all day long! Next time I'll go with skim milk because it's very rich.

This recipe was amazing! I never knew butternut squash could taste so good. My family loved it also. I will make it again, but this time I will either omit the top long cook lasagna noodles or cook they first. It’s no big deal but for some reason, the top lasagna noodles or crispy/hard. I also added sautéed spinach for color & mozzarella cheese like some of the reviewers suggested. I believe the key to this exceptional recipe is adding the right amount of salt and pepper which I did, thank God, because I taste tested after I added the butternut squash to the cream/milk mixture.

I roasted both the garlic and butternut squash and together in the cream sauce they create an incredible flavor. It's luscious! While the squash was roasting in the oven, I put dry noodles in a 9 x 13 pan on the stove and poured HOT water over them. They were soft by the time the squash came out of the oven! I made the white sauce with nonfat milk and used fat free half and half on top. I also chopped fresh spinach and put it in each layer. This dish is perfect for a casual family dinner or as a side dish for a more sophisticated dinner party. I give it 10 stars!

I tried this recipe last night and it was excellent! I did make a few modifications after reading the suggestions by others. 

I added a whole bag of frozen spinach to add color and nutrition; I put the spinach on top of the 2nd layer of sauce. 

I also took the suggestion of adding onion. I did this by sauteeing a whole chopped yellow onion in the butter, before adding the garlic for another 1-2 minutes. 

I also added about 1/2 tsp of cayenne pepper to the sauce- an excellent suggestion from my husband! 

I didn't whip the cream before pouring it on top- perhaps the reason for a few crunchy noodles on top. 

We are healthy omnivores and we did NOT find this dish at all bland, and it was not overly rich. I will definitely be making this dish again!

I have made this several times. I have never put the heavy cream mix on and don't miss it at all. I have made a few small changes. I layer in the following manner - squash sauce, noodles, sauce, parm, noodles, basil pesto, mozzarella, noodles, sauce, parm, noodles, sauce, mozzarella and parm. My family can't wait to have this.

I made this tonight and it was really good but it is rich. I, like many others, tweaked the recipe some. I sauteed the garlic, onions and mushrooms and then added that to the butternut squash. I also added nutmeg to the sauce like several suggested. I also layered with fresh spinach and it was really good. To cut some calories I used fat free half and half so I just poured it over the top, but next time I will make a little extra butternut squash filling and put that on top with some cheese. I will definately make again!

I made this exactly as stated in the recipe and my family enjoyed it but it was too rich/heavy for me. Made it again this Christmas with a few adjustments, and it came out perfect (for me). I added one onion, and doubled the garlic. And following the other recommendations, added a bag of fresh spinach, increased the amount of butter nut squash, but the best tweak of all, adding a 5 ounce package of fresh basil! This is a great recipe, and easy to adjust to your particular taste!
Just okay. A little one note re flavor and texture. I'll keep hunting for a great seasonal lasagna.

This turned out amazing! It did take longer than indicated, somewhere between 3-3 1/2 hours. I believe that in part was mostly due to the size of the squash which was probably closer to 4 lbs and therefore took a little over an hour to cook in order to be soft enough to scoop. I did add an half a sweet onion to the butter/garlic mix because I had to use it up but otherwise followed the recipe to a T. Everyone loved it and went back for seconds. I would definitely make again but probably just for special occasions considering the time involved. Absolutely delicious!

I left off the whipped cream, and it was still delicious. I will make this again. As a vegetarian, it reminds me of the butternut raviolis I often get as the vegetarian option at a banquet, only much better.

Oh, man! No one knew what I made, and I understand their confusion. This amazing recipe is almost life-changing. I was cooking for a group and wanted something different, and the combination of garlic and butternut squash sounded perfect. I live in Central America, and couldn't find squash, so used sweet potatoes and can't imagine it would make a huge amount of difference. Otherwise, I pretty much just followed the directions. By the time the sauce was done and I tasted it, I knew I had a winner. I will make this again in the future, but probably without the lasagna noodles. I'm thinking serving it with noodles and chicken, maybe mushrooms, maybe broccoli. Or just make it for myself and sit in the kitchen with a big old spoon and eat it right from the bowl. Its that good!

I should have taken a photo....I have a recipe like this from years ago, almost exactly the same, so made this one, but added fontina cheese to it. I added some rosemary as well and up'd the roasted garlic. Good recipe. You can forget the lasagna noodles and simply stir in cooked macaroni for a mac n cheese type dish. This is a good dish, have been making it for a long time and every time I serve it, its well loved!
Amazing! Added onions and nutmeg to garlic mix and mozzarella to layering. So good.
One of the tastiest no-meat lasagnas I have ever made.
Love this recipe! We added a layer of spinach and mozzarella cheese! Amazing! Thanks for sharing!

I have made this recipe twice. The prep time is much longer than the 30 minutes stated. The sauce takes at least 20 minutes to cook down and I added 2-3 additional tablespoons of flour to get it to thicken. However, this is a delicious and versatile recipe. The first time, I added onion and spinach. The second time, I also added mushrooms and red pepper. I did not use the cream on top, just some of the sauce and some mozzarella cheese. Depending on what you put in it, and how much chopping you need to do, allow at least 2-3 hours, not counting the bake time for the squash.
